record.title: A targeted SFT and RL routing study reports gains on a bounded set of enterprise analytics skills
record.summary: A preprint studies how to allocate supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) for long-horizon analytics agents using production-mirroring beta APIs. It separates retrospectively observed trajectories into imitation, lift and discovery regimes, then uses teacher support and reward-observable headroom to route features to SFT, RL or further environment work. Across 18 subsequent feature-specific experiments, the diagnostic reportedly predicted 15 trajectories. On GPT-OSS 120B, targeted SFT-then-RL produced positive point estimates on seven of eight advertiser skills versus a frontier control; five gains had paired 95% confidence intervals excluding zero and one skill had a supported regression. A matched comparison reports a higher seven-skill mean delta with 43% less incremental RL compute than uniform routing.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ experiments, the routing diagnostic predicted 15/18 feature trajectories; targeted SFT-then-RL on GPT-OSS 120B had positive point estimates on 7/8 advertiser skills, with five paired 95% intervals excluding zero, and the matched targeted-versus-uniform comparison reported a seven-skill mean delta of +3.57 versus +1.62 using 43% less incremental RL compute.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper’s author-reported results do not establish independent reproduction or broader deployment impact.

evidence_gaps.description: The feature-routing results and reported compute comparison have not been independently reproduced outside the authors’ analytics environment.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated in other tasks, routing training effort by teacher coverage and observable reward headroom could improve the return on post-training compute. The measured setting is specialized enterprise advertising analytics, and most outcomes remain paper-reported.
limitations: The experiments concern advertiser skills in one enterprise analytics environment and do not establish transfer to other agent tasks.
Results are author-reported; the research desk did not reproduce the API environment or training runs.
The paper reports a supported regression on one of eight skills; averages do not imply uniform benefit.

brief.title: A targeted SFT and RL routing study reports gains on a bounded set of enterprise analytics skills
brief.why_it_matters: The paper offers a potentially useful way to decide where RL is worth its extra compute in tool-using workflows. The evidence comes from one enterprise analytics setting and author-run experiments, so it does not establish a general training recipe or field-wide efficiency gain.
